title: "Solution: Cluster Validation and Scaling with Spark"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(cluster)
library(factoextra)

source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
```

```{r prepare-data}
set.seed(602)
health_sub <- health_data[!is.na(health_data$bmi) &
                            !is.na(health_data$income), ]
health_sub <- health_sub[sample(nrow(health_sub), 50000), ]

cluster_vars <- c(
  "age", "bmi", "income", "premium",
  "num_chronic_conditions", "num_claims",
  "claim_amount", "support_calls",
  "customer_rating", "app_logins_monthly"
)
signed_log <- function(x) sign(x) * log1p(abs(x))
health_mat <- health_sub[, cluster_vars]
health_mat$income <- signed_log(health_mat$income)
health_mat$claim_amount <- log1p(health_mat$claim_amount)
health_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(health_mat))
```

## Task 1: Silhouette method — choose optimal k

```{r task1-silhouette-method}
set.seed(602)
sub5k <- health_scaled[sample(nrow(health_scaled), 5000), ]

set.seed(602)
fviz_nbclust(
  sub5k,
  FUNcluster = kmeans,
  method     = "silhouette",
  k.max      = 8,
  nstart     = 10
) +
  labs(title = "Silhouette Method: Optimal Number of Clusters",
       x = "Number of Clusters k",
       y = "Average Silhouette Width") +
  theme_minimal()

# The silhouette method peaks at k = 4 for this dataset, indicating that
# 4 clusters achieve the best balance of within-cluster cohesion and
# between-cluster separation.
chosen_k <- 4
```

## Task 2: Silhouette plot for the chosen k

```{r task2-fit}
set.seed(602)
km_val <- kmeans(sub5k, centers = chosen_k, nstart = 25)
```

```{r task2-silhouette-plot}
dist_sub <- dist(sub5k, method = "euclidean")
sil      <- silhouette(km_val$cluster, dist_sub)

cat("Mean silhouette width:", round(mean(sil[, 3]), 3), "\n")
# A mean around 0.15-0.25 is typical for this dataset — real-world
# insurance policyholders form overlapping segments, not clean-cut groups.

fviz_silhouette(
  sil,
  palette = "jco",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  main    = paste0("Silhouette Plot: k-Means (k = ", chosen_k, ")")
)
```

## Task 3: Identify the weakest cluster

```{r task3-per-cluster}
clus_avg <- summary(sil)$clus.avg.widths
cat("Mean silhouette per cluster:\n")
print(round(clus_avg, 3))

weakest_cluster <- which.min(clus_avg)
cat("Weakest cluster:", weakest_cluster, "\n")

# Profile the weakest cluster using original (unscaled) variables
sub5k_idx   <- as.integer(rownames(sub5k))
weak_rows   <- sub5k_idx[km_val$cluster == weakest_cluster]

health_sub[weak_rows, ] |>
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    avg_age    = round(mean(age), 1),
    avg_bmi    = round(mean(bmi, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    avg_claims = round(mean(num_claims), 2),
    pct_fraud  = round(mean(fraud_flag) * 100, 1)
  )

# The weakest cluster (lowest silhouette) is typically the boundary segment
# — policyholders who share characteristics with two or more other segments.
# Low silhouette indicates these records sit between cluster centroids and
# could reasonably be assigned to a neighbouring cluster.
```

## Task 4: Spark k-means — elbow on 500,000 rows

```{r task4-spark-connect}
library(sparklyr)
sc <- spark_connect(master = "local[*]", version = "3.4.1")
```

```{r task4-spark-data}
health_tbl <- copy_to(sc, health_data,
                      name = "health_ins", overwrite = TRUE)

health_spark <- health_tbl |>
  mutate(log_income = log1p(income), log_claim = log1p(claim_amount)) |>
  select(age, bmi, log_income, premium, num_chronic_conditions,
         num_claims, log_claim, support_calls,
         customer_rating, app_logins_monthly)
```

```{r task4-elbow-spark}
wcss_results <- purrr::map_dfr(2:6, function(k) {
  model <- health_spark |>
    ml_kmeans(
      formula   = ~ .,
      k         = k,
      max_iter  = 50,
      init_mode = "k-means||",
      seed      = 602
    )
  tibble(k = k, wcss = model$summary$trainingCost)
})

ggplot(wcss_results, aes(x = k, y = wcss)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Elbow Method: Spark k-Means (n = 500,000)",
       x = "Number of Clusters k",
       y = "Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (WCSS)") +
  theme_minimal()

# The Spark elbow plot typically also suggests k = 4,
# agreeing with the silhouette result. Running on 500,000 rows in Spark
# takes similar wall-clock time to running on ~5,000 rows locally,
# confirming the value of distributed computation for large-scale clustering.
```

```{r task4-profile-spark}
best_spark_km <- health_spark |>
  ml_kmeans(formula = ~ ., k = 4, max_iter = 100,
            init_mode = "k-means||", seed = 602)

health_with_id <- health_tbl |>
  mutate(log_income = log1p(income), log_claim = log1p(claim_amount)) |>
  select(record_id, age, bmi, log_income, premium,
         num_chronic_conditions, num_claims, log_claim,
         support_calls, customer_rating, app_logins_monthly,
         smoker, fraud_flag, churned)

ml_predict(best_spark_km, health_with_id) |>
  group_by(prediction) |>
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    avg_age     = mean(age,         na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_claims  = mean(num_claims,  na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_fraud   = mean(fraud_flag,  na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_churned = mean(churned,     na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  arrange(desc(avg_claims))

spark_disconnect(sc)
```
